title.suggested: Saloon rounds on the eve of the McCoole–Allen fight

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican reported on the eve of the McCoole–Allen fight that both men, arrested Sunday night and freed on $1,000 peace bonds, were fit, with little betting and order promised on the boat.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'The Missouri Republican, St. Louis, Tuesday, September 23, 1873', page 5.

facts.fact: Allen was arrested by detectives on Sunday night at a temporary training place, the 'Hunter's Retreat' near Jefferson Barracks, while McCoole was arrested at his training quarters
places: Hunter's Retreat, near Jefferson Barracks, Missouri

facts.fact: Allen and McCoole were released from the Four Courts on bail of $1,000 each to keep the peace in Missouri for three months; Jack Looney spent the night getting Allen free
The Allen–McCoole fight was set for the day of publication, with spectators taken by boat and both men to be picked up on the way
Arthur Chambers, champion light-weight, and Patsy Sheppard were in St. Louis and expected to second Allen

notes: Pre-fight report, not fight coverage; current title implies the fight itself. Allen's saloon is described with a concert room and his colors (Brummagem blue and white bird's-eye) hung beside Gallagher's green and gold.
